browser: Pinned Google Chrome 154, loopback-only real HTTP responses; no Playwright route/fulfill interception.

cases.purpose: Observe actual Chrome Back behavior for an otherwise eligible no-store HTML response.
Fresh-GET control. A test-only unload listener excludes BFCache; no-store also prevents an HTTP cache hit. This does not claim no-store alone forces a GET.

postCases.purpose: Back from a following GET to a cacheable actual POST response while BFCache is eligible.
Fresh-response control: a test-only unload listener on the POST response excludes BFCache, allowing observation of browser HTTP-cache/session-history behavior without assuming a repeated POST.

notes.partialDate: The test clears an actual date input then types a partial segment through Chrome keyboard input. Capture records value, badInput, activeElement, and screenshots; it does not fake the browser's inaccessible segment buffer.
notes.freshGetControl: Chrome may BFCache no-store documents. The separate unload-listener case is explicitly a control for observing restoration after a genuine new GET; response headers and server receipts distinguish it from BFCache.
notes.additionalState: Password with default autocomplete and autocomplete=off, date with default autocomplete, pristine and edited-back-to-default dates, untouched default, edited-back-to-default text, multiple select, checkbox, radio group, and range are exercised through browser actions. Disabled/readonly values are script-mutated for same-document identification only, not as a production scripting recommendation.
notes.postCache: POST result responses carry explicit public freshness and Content-Location equal to the response URL. Both POST and later GET requests are recorded; no response is fulfilled by Playwright.
